candidates.statement: [44] If X1, X2 are any two repre- sentations of the same sequence of objects in a monoidal category C, then there is a unique isomorphism between ⊗(X1) and ⊗(X2) consisting of compositions of α, l, r ′s. We call the unique isomorphism in Theorem 2.1.1 a canonical isomorphism. A monoidal category (C, ⊗, 1, α, l, r) is sometimes written as C for simplicity. A monoidal category C is deﬁned to be strict if all the α, l, r ′s are identity maps, namely, the canonical isomorphism between diﬀerent representations are actually the Section 2.1 Ribbon Fusion Categories identity. Another theorem of Mac Lane shows that every monoidal category is monoidal
